title: Eldercare providers commonly link to non-household recipients, but annual samples cannot show burden or displacement
source_unit: ATUS respondent age 15+ with at least one eldercare-roster record and final respondent weight

observations.period: 2024; provider respondents with at least one listed recipient

listed_recipients_per_provider.unit: weighted mean listed recipient records per provider respondent

observations.method: Eldercare roster records linked to the 2024 ATUS respondent/activity frame by TUCASEID; provider-level indicators weighted by respondent final weight. Recipient records are not independently weighted.
observations.uncertainty: Descriptive weighted annual estimate; no replicate-weight standard errors are reproduced for the roster indicators. Roster reporting and recipient multiplicity remain relevant limits.
observations.subgroup: ATUS respondents with at least one eldercare-roster record in 2024.
observations.counterinterpretation: A listed non-household recipient does not measure distance, care hours, burden, relationship quality, or whether support was shared with other caregivers.

observations.period: 2025; provider respondents with at least one listed recipient

listed_recipients_per_provider.unit: weighted mean listed recipient records per provider respondent

observations.method: Same TUCASEID linkage and respondent-weighted provider indicators as the 2024 observation, applied to the 2025 ATUS files.
observations.uncertainty: Descriptive weighted annual comparison; 2024 and 2025 are separate annual samples, not the same respondents, and no roster-specific replicate-weight standard errors are reproduced.
observations.subgroup: ATUS respondents with at least one eldercare-roster record in 2025.
observations.counterinterpretation: The small annual movement in listed-recipient multiplicity or recipient type may reflect sample composition, reporting, or roster structure; it does not establish a trend in care burden or work displacement.

boundary: This is a repeated annual population comparison, not a panel of the same providers or recipients. It separates household and non-household recipient links but does not measure care intensity, travel, paid or unpaid substitution, schedule control, recipient outcomes, recovery, trust, political action, or causality. Recipient rows are not independently weighted.
